text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Monday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Police cordons withdraw after eight days of round-the-clock student protests in Belgrade over annulment of local election results.
- Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic to meet Russian deputy foreign minister Igor Ivanov. Ivanov conveys Russia's concern about events in Serbia.
- Ethnic Albanian representatives at Serbian-Albanian talks in Munich disagree with theory that change of regime and democratisation in Serbia would resolve the question of Kosovo.
- The Hague tribunal will ask Yugoslav authorities for exact information about which courts are dealing with specific war crimes cases, says chief prosecutor Louise Arbour after visit to Belgrade.
- Food prices still rising. Price of cooking oil expected to go up in March.
- Under new draft Serbian law on privatisation, firms will be able to decide themselves whether to privatise or stay "socially owned". Shares to be sold at a discount to employees.
- UNHCR appeals to Bosnia-Herzegovina and Croatia to enable easier return of refugees.
- Trichinosis spreading in Serbia. In Loznica region 92 cases registered.

- "We will stay in the government because radical reforms have been announced," says Dusan Mihajlovic, president of New Democracy, one of the parties in the ruling coalition. "Zajedno opposition coalition's biggest minus is that they do not know what they are for -- monarchy or a republic, secession or keeping of Kosovo, civic or national options."
- Serbian Radical Party leader Vojislav Seselj in talks with Russian Duma delegation says Zajedno coalition under the west's influence, working against their own people.

- More liberal imports of foreign goods hurting domestic industry which needs support to recover from the effects of sanctions, says management of household appliance manufacturer Elektronska Industrija (EI) Nis.
- Independent trade unions of 11 firms of the Belgrade metal complex announce protests outside Serbian government on February 3rd unless late wages are paid by then.
- Two photographers and one other person injured when a car ran into crowd during student and opposition protests in Belgrade Sunday evening.
